subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks again for your time this morning. Quick recap of what we discussed and recommended next steps so your team has a clean reference: 

1) Summary of Nova Health needs we heard
- High-concurrency inference for triage and patient-note summarization (peak ~600 reqs/s)
- PHI-handling requirement for some pipelines (HIPAA scope)
- Preference to minimize downtime and keep model behavior consistent during migration

2) Deployment modes we mapped to your constraints
- Hosted API: fastest to try (no infra), good for non-PHI or low-risk workloads, pay-as-you-go.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (SLA-backed), predictable throughput for production traffic, data isolation within Redwood Dedicated tenancy.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): full network control, KMS/HSM integrations, suitable for PHI and strict procurement requirements.

3) Migration options from your current setup (self-hosted / legacy GPU cluster / other API)
- Hybrid approach: start with Hosted API for quick validation (non-PHI), then move sensitive pipelines to Dedicated or Private while we pre-warm KV caches and match prompt/eval sets.
- Direct migration to Dedicated/Private: preferred if procurement timeline allows and you need capacity guarantees on day one.

4) Action items / next steps
- Dev: can you review Nova’s network diagram and confirm VPC peering options? (cc: Dev)
- Sofia: confirm which pipelines will process PHI vs. non-PHI so we can propose a split migration plan.
- Marissa/Rachel: we’ll send an initial SOW draft and a short comparison doc (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) by EOD tomorrow.

I’ve attached a short comparison doc and a template SOW to get the conversation started.

Attachments: deployment_modes_comparison.pdf, redwood_sow_draft_v1.docx

Thanks — look forward to continuing the momentum.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alan Chu <alan.chu@novahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2027 13:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Marissa — really helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- We have two pipelines that will definitely process PHI (clinical notes ingestion and discharge summaries). Those need to be in a private or dedicated environment.
- Remaining services (summaries for patient-facing FAQs and analytics) can live in hosted while we validate performance.
- Our current infra is a legacy GPU cluster running a mix of open models and an API layer. We expect a 6–8 week migration window for core models (we want no more than 48 hours of disruption).

Questions: 
1) For Dedicated, can you confirm the SLA for p95 latency and uptime? (we need numbers for procurement)
2) For Private VPC option — what is the typical network setup? Do you support VPC peering + private link to avoid egress?
3) If we go hybrid (hosted -> dedicated/private), can you help with KV-cache warmup and rolling model parity testing to avoid regressions?

Can your engineering lead join a tech deep-dive on Wed? Alan (cc) will coordinate schedules.

Regards,
Sofia
Director of AI Platform
Nova Health
sofia.ramirez@novahealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sofia — great, thanks for the detail. Short answers and proposed schedule: 

- Dedicated SLA: we guarantee 99.9% monthly uptime for Dedicated clusters and p95 token-generation latency SLAs are configurable by workload class — I’ll attach the SLA appendix; summary: p95 < 350ms for standard gen models under provisioned throughput. Procurement will ask for exact language; we’ll supply the appendix and service credits clause in the SOW.

- Private VPC: yes — we support VPC peering and private link options. We can also deploy the private control plane in your VPC with customer-managed network ingress. We’ll provide a network checklist.

- Cache warmup & parity testing: yes. Our migration playbook includes staged warmups (prefix caching + shadow traffic) and eval suites to compare outputs. We’ll coordinate a 2-week parity test window before cutover.

Proposed timeline (high-level):
Week 1: Hosted pilot for non-PHI workloads + tech deep-dive (Wed)
Weeks 2–3: Dedicated sizing & procurement (if chosen) / network prep for Private
Weeks 4–7: Parallel testing, KV warmup, QA, and canary switchovers
Week 8: Final cutover for core models

Dev, can you confirm network checklist items and whether Nova’s current cluster can export model artifacts or if we need an exporter?

I’ve attached an updated SOW draft and the deployment comparison doc with more details.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ramirez <sofia.ramirez@novahealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2027 10:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Deployment mode & migration plan (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Hi Sofia — quick technical notes ahead of the Wed deep-dive. I’m attaching a short worksheet that maps our network checklist to common Nova setups. Highlights: 

1) Network & connectivity\- VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink are both supported. For Private deployments we recommend PrivateLink to avoid cross-VPC routing complexity; peering works if CIDR ranges don’t clash.

2) Data ingress and PHI handling\- For PHI pipelines we recommend Dedicated with encrypted egress + customer-managed KMS if you want key control. For Private on-prem, we support HSM integrations. We do not persist raw input by default; we can enable configurable retention for audit windows.

3) Model artifacts and export\- If you can export model artifacts (weights + tokenizer + config) we’ll run a compatibility check and a one-time conversion. If not, we can re-host compatible open-model variants and run a QA parity suite. Typical artifact export format: torch + safetensors or HF tarball.

4) KV cache warmup strategy\- We support prefix caching and replaying logs to pre-populate KV cache. For a 48-hour cutover SLA, we’d recommend a 48–72 hour warmup window with shadow traffic of ~10–20% of production to build caches.

5) Attachments included: nova_health_network_requirements.xlsx (network checklist + sample CIDR), deployment_modes_comparison.pdf (comparison table), redwood_sow_draft_v1.docx (SOW draft).

I’ll be on the Wed call — if you can share an export sample or a small model manifest before then that would help us size the conversion work.

Cheers,
Dev Patel
Staff Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.ai
